text:
maria: Heads up - seeing odd saturation in eu-west. One GPU pod at ~98% util while others are 10-20% and queue length is growing. Admission latency up to 6s.

dan: Can you paste the scheduler metrics query you ran?

maria: ran this: `sum by(node) (gpu_utilization)` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(admission_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]))` - 95th jumped from 120ms -> 6s around 03:12 UTC.

kevin: I pulled scheduler queue snapshot (from /debug/queue):
```
queue: 312 pending
oldest_request_age_seconds: 74
top-5: [req-5432(age=74,priority=medium), req-3121(age=73,priority=low), req-9990(age=72,priority=high), ...]
```
Looks like a single long-running request (req-5432) at head is blocking admission because comparator returns stable ordering that favors older small jobs on the same shard.

anya: That smells like head-of-line blocking but at the scheduler level — if we don't preempt or requeue we get hotspots. Any recent scheduler commits?

dan: There was a change two days ago to the comparator in the priority queue (PR 842) to handle fairness; it may be inadvertently sorting by submit_time only and not taking expected_gpu_seconds into account. Working hypothesis: huge batch requests with older submit_time get stuck at front, blocking many small low-latency requests for other nodes -> uneven GPU packing.

maria: Repro command I used: `curl -s $SCHED/debug/queue | jq .top[0:10]` - happy to share output privately.

kevin: Quick mitigation: lowering admission_threshold on router from 0.85 -> 0.6 and enabling cross-node spillover allowed small requests to go to spare nodes. I rolled that change to canary 2/6 routers. Immediate effect: tail latency fell to ~180ms and GPU hotspots smoothed.

infra-oncall: rolled restart of scheduler-1 pod at 03:40 UTC to pick up recent hotfix config (no deploy, just restart). Observed scheduler rebalancing: pending queue dropped from 312 -> 87 within 90s.

sre-bot: incident:alert: scheduler_queue_high - 1799991111 - triggered at 03:12 UTC. tagging eng-infra, oncall.

anya: We need a proper fix not just threshold fiddling. Dan, can you confirm comparator logic? If it's sorting by submit_time only we should change it to use a composite key: (expected_gpu_seconds DESC, submit_time ASC) or use dynamic aging.

dan: Yep, found the bug: comparator used `a.submit_time < b.submit_time || a.id < b.id` in SchedulerQueue.less(), missing any cost term. PR 896 implements prioritized cost-aware ordering + unit tests. Also added a metric `queue_head_cost` to detect cost-heavy heads.

maria: Tests look good in my local, ran synthetic load with mixed small/large requests - throughput improved and tail latency stable.

kevin: What's the rollout plan? We should canary in us-east and eu-west routers and watch `gpu_utilization` and `admission_latency` for 30m before global rollout. Also plan a quick fallback (disable new comparator via feature flag).

anya: Agreed. Steps: 1) merge PR 896, 2) build and tag canary image, 3) deploy to scheduler-canary (us-east), 4) watch metrics for 30m, 5) deploy to eu-west, then rest. I'll own the rollout.

infra-oncall: started canary deploy to us-east at 04:20 UTC (scheduler:v2026-03-04-canary). Will post updates.

maria: After canary patch: us-east 95p admission latency down from 2.1s -> 160ms, GPU spread even. eu-west canary ongoing.

dan: PR merged to main at 05:05 UTC. Added changelog, rollback flag `SCHED_COMPARATOR=v1|v2`.

kevin: Postmortem notes: root cause = comparator change that lost cost-awareness -> head-of-queue high-cost jobs blocked many small ones -> uneven GPU packing and effective capacity reduction. Action items: add e2e for mixed-workload scheduling, add alert on queue_head_cost > X, and run chaos test for admission backpressure.

anya: I'll create the postmortem draft and assign owners for the three action items. Thanks all for quick triage :thumbsup:

maria: leaving logs and the jq output in the incident folder: https://redwood/sops/incidents/1799991111-queue-backpressure.

infra-oncall: closing the incident thread once eu-west fully rolled out and metrics stable for 1h.
